# Hello Clause

Hello Clause provides one reusable action, `say`, which writes text to a configured document location and emits a `Hello Said` event. Named connections under `bindings.say` determine how it is invoked; this type declares no automatic connection.

## Text and action effects

`bindings.text` is required and must be a non-root JSON Pointer: Text beginning with `/`, other than `/` itself. It identifies the destination in the document where the clause executes. There is no default binding path or initial text value.

The action parameter `text` defaults to `"Hello World"`. Parameter resolution starts with this default, merges the workflow request object when `input:true`, and then applies connection `params`. Workflow `inputParams` and then `documentParams` can override individual parameter paths using existing request and document values. Their mapping keys are target pointers and their values are source pointers; both must be non-root pointers. Missing projected values leave earlier values unchanged. `input` defaults to `false`.

After the connection guards pass, any `before` steps run. The action then requires `params.text` to be Text, rejecting otherwise with `Hello text must be Text`. It stages a `replace` at `bindings.text` and emits `Hello Said`, whose `clause` identifies the clause key, `connection` identifies the invoking connection, and `text` contains the resolved text. Any `after` steps follow these effects. An attempted invocation alone does not establish committed effects, and `Hello Said` does not establish delivery or acknowledgement by a person.

`"Hello World"` is an invocation default, not the value of missing document state. An absent destination value is unknown.

## Connections and guards

A connection's `on` selects `workflow`, `event`, `channel`, `embedded`, `collection`, `change`, `initialized`, `activated` or `timer`. `initialized` selects `Clauses Initialized`; `activated` selects `Document Activated`. Path-based sources require a non-root `path`. Collection connections accept source paths beneath that collection path. Embedded and collection sources also contribute their paths for embedding unless `embed:false`.

Workflow connections use `party`, falling back to `channel`; channel sources name an existing channel. Hello Clause fixes no particular actor or caller permission. Workflow `requireExactDocumentVersion` defaults to `false`; when enabled, the call must also carry that flag as `true`, or execution rejects with `EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`.

Connection `when` defaults to `true`; a false result skips execution. `parameters.conditions.say` also defaults to `true`, and every applicable `parameters.conditionGroups` condition must pass. A group's missing `condition` defaults to `false`; supplied `inputs` are available as `conditionInputs`. Failed action conditions reject with `ACTION_CONDITION_FAILED`. A connection `profile` selects an entry from `parameters.connectionProfiles` containing only `params` and `when`; using a profile together with local `params` or `when` is rejected.

`once` defaults to `false`. With `once:true`, a recorded `fired:true` skips later invocations of that connection. The flag is set after the action and its `after` steps finish. Repeatable connections do not set it, so `fired:false` does not establish that `say` has never run. Connection initialization supplies `fired:false` and `armed:false`; absent flags remain unknown.

Clause and connection names must be nonempty Text without `.`, `/` or `~`. Changing an installed clause's configuration requires a new clause key under the inherited transition check.

## Optional timers

A timer connection requires exactly one of `timestamp` and `afterEvent`. An absolute `timestamp` is a nonnegative integer Unix-microsecond deadline, at most `9007199254740991`; it arms on initialization and forbids `delayMs` and `policy`. A relative timer requires a timestamped source rather than initialization, plus positive integer `delayMs` in milliseconds, at most `9007199254740`. Its deadline derives from the source timestamp and must remain within the timestamp bound.

Relative `policy` defaults to `first`, which ignores later arming sources once `armed` is true. `latest` emits replacement requests for the same pending timer key. The clause never clears `armed` on firing or cancellation, so it records arming rather than current pending status. Optional `cancelOn` emits a cancellation request; committed cancellation cannot undo an earlier firing.

Timers require explicitly selected Time runtime support. Emitting a scheduling request is not a firing, and emitting a cancellation request alone is not confirmation of cancellation. Firing depends on committed registration and authoritative input-history evidence; processing may occur after the requested deadline. New deadlines must follow the invocation's logical position, except that standalone initialization without a prior external position may request an already elapsed absolute deadline.
